newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields lower, crown loses to dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields lower, crown loses to dollar.

text.p: Swedish bond yields remained lower in Tuesday morning trade while the crown firmed against the mark but kept falling against the dollar.
"The crown is holding up against the mark awaiting something to happen. It's the dollar and sterling that are moving otherwise it's quite calm," one dealer said.
"Most people seem to think the dollar will head further up, but it's difficult to say."
The crown firmed to 4.4240 against the mark from 4.4395 late on Monday. Against the dollar the crown fell to 7.3889 versus 7.3394 late Monday.
Nine-year bond yields dropped three basis point to 6.66 percent in early trade, driven lower by German yields, but rose two basis points to 6.68 percent by midday.
Six-month T-bill rates slipped to 4.02 percent in earloy trade but rose later rose two basis points to 4.04 percent compared to late Monday.
As expected Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, left its key interest rate, the repo rate, unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly reverse repurchase operation.
